input_signals.name: Persistent Innovation Low-Noise
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms combining sustained R&D investment with a stable earnings-to-cash reconciliation subsequently earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Cumulative R&D intensity identifies a persistent investment program rather than a one-period spending spike. Low volatility in accrual intensity indicates that the program is accompanied by less accounting noise, helping separate repeatable innovation investment from unstable accrual-driven earnings.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), ts_sum( sale, 5 ) ) ), rank( neg( vol( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible-Scaled Working-Capital Mismatch
input_signals.expression: MUL(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), RATIO(intan, at)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Positive working-capital accruals predict especially low returns as a firm's expensed and booked intangible footprint increases.
input_signals.reasoning: Intangible-based business models should generally require less incremental working capital, so a large buildup is more anomalous when the intangible footprint is high. The continuous intangible weight preserves cross-sectional variation and makes the long and short tails reflect opposing working-capital outcomes among intangible firms without hard-zeroing most observations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sumrank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), ratio( intan, at ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( wcap, 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Nonoverlapping R&D Cash Realization
input_signals.hypothesis: A completed period of persistent R&D investment followed by a subsequent improvement in cash flow relative to accounting earnings predicts higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Lagging the three-period R&D window by three periods makes it nonoverlapping with the current three-period cash-reconciliation trend, implementing a genuine investment-then-realization sequence. Using a subsequent trend rather than a one-period change should also reduce noisy portfolio turnover and strengthen alignment between the cross-sectional slope and long-short evidence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( lag( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 3 ) ), rank( winsor( trend( ratio( sub( oancf, ib ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Identifiable-Intangible Amortization Shortfall
input_signals.hypothesis: Prior additions to identifiable intangible assets predict lower returns when they are followed by declining depreciation and amortization recognition.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the previously repeated cash-validation leg with a lead-lag test of whether capitalized identifiable intangibles generate the expected subsequent noncash expense. A high score identifies firms adding non-goodwill intangible assets while reducing depreciation and amortization, consistent with delayed expense recognition rather than conservative accounting.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( lag( ratio( delta( sub( intan, gdwl ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( neg( delta( ratio( dp, at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Expensing-Regime Cash Funding Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms using an R&D-heavy expensing regime and maintaining a strong operating-cash floor subsequently earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal selects one coherent accounting regime—immediate R&D expensing—rather than averaging it with the conceptually opposed booked-intangible regime. Conditioning that expense mix on the worst recent operating-cash outcome distinguishes sustainably funded innovation from firms whose high R&D share simply reflects weak depreciable capital or reporter status.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), add( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), ts_sum( dp, 3 ) ) ) ), rank( ts_min( winsor( ratio( oancf, at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liability-Adjusted Expensing Cash Floor
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), TS_SUM(dp, 3)))), RANK(TS_MIN(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, apalch), txach), at), 1), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms using an R&D-heavy expensing regime and maintaining strong operating cash flow after removing payable and tax-accrual financing subsequently earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The strong expensing-regime cash-floor result may partly reflect operating cash temporarily boosted by unpaid suppliers or accrued taxes. Removing those liability changes tests whether the innovation program is supported by internally realized cash rather than by working-capital financing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), add( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), ts_sum( dp, 3 ) ) ) ), rank( ts_min( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, apalch ), txach ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Post-Innovation Cash-Reconciliation Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: A completed period of persistent R&D investment followed by consistently cash-supported earnings predicts higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Prior nonoverlapping signals show that cash improvement after R&D has strong cross-sectional and portfolio evidence. Using the subsequent period's minimum cash-minus-earnings outcome tests whether that realization is durable rather than driven by a single favorable endpoint or trend estimate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( lag( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 3 ) ), rank( ts_min( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, ib ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Gross-Profit Cash Conversion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), TS_SUM(dp, 3)))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(oancf, 3), TS_SUM(SUB(sale, cogs), 3)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with an R&D-heavy expense regime and high conversion of gross profit into operating cash flow subsequently earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Scaling operating cash by gross profit asks whether the economic margin associated with innovation is actually realized in cash, rather than rewarding cash profitability relative to assets. Three-period aggregation reduces sensitivity to annual working-capital timing and aligns the cash horizon with the expense-mix measure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), add( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), ts_sum( dp, 3 ) ) ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( oancf, 3 ), ts_sum( sub( sale, cogs ), 3 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Cash-Absorption Capacity
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms that retain substantial operating cash flow after absorbing their innovation spending subsequently earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The first leg requires economically meaningful intangible investment, while the second measures whether operating cash remains large relative to that R&D burden. Because greater R&D mechanically makes the cash-coverage ratio harder to satisfy, the interaction separates sustainably funded innovation from a simple R&D-intensity or cash-profitability effect.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ), ts_sum( sale, 3 ) ) ), rank( ratio( ts_sum( oancf, 3 ), add( abs( ts_sum( oancf, 3 ) ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dual Expense Compression
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms simultaneously reducing R&D expense intensity and depreciation and amortization expense subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Both changes mechanically increase current accounting earnings without requiring improved operating cash generation. The interaction therefore targets coordinated compression of immediately expensed and noncash long-lived investment costs rather than recombining an R&D accounting-regime score with another archived cash-floor measure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( winsor( delta( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ), rank( neg( winsor( delta( ratio( dp, at ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Adjusted Innovation Margin
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)), RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(recch, invch)), sale), 1), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms whose gross margins remain strong after receivables and inventory cash absorption subsequently earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding recch and invch to gross profit correctly reduces the margin when receivables or inventory build and increases it when those operating assets release cash. This replaces the unstable cash-to-gross-profit ratio with a sales-scaled realization margin, avoiding sign-flipped scores for negative-gross-profit firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ), rank( ma( winsor( ratio( add( sub( sale, cogs ), add( recch, invch ) ), sale ), 1 ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Pre-Working-Capital Cash Generation
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)), RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, recch), invch), at), 1), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with strong operating cash generation before receivables and inventory timing effects subsequently earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Removing recch and invch from operating cash reverses both temporary cash boosts from asset liquidation and temporary cash drains from commercialization-related asset investment. The signal therefore tests whether innovation is supported by underlying operating cash generation rather than applying another downside operator to an archived bounded-coverage measure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ), rank( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, recch ), invch ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Incremental R&D Commercialization Payback
input_signals.expression: ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(DELTA(SUB(sale, cogs), 1), ADD(recch, invch)), ADD(ABS(ADD(DELTA(SUB(sale, cogs), 1), ADD(recch, invch))), LAG(xrd, 1))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating large receivables- and inventory-adjusted gross-profit improvements relative to prior R&D spending subsequently earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The numerator measures incremental gross profit after penalizing receivables and inventory accumulation, while prior R&D supplies the economically relevant investment base. This is an incremental payback ratio rather than a window or output-leg substitution on the archived R&D-intensity interactions.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: zscore( winsor( ratio( add( delta( sub( sale, cogs ), 1 ), add( recch, invch ) ), add( abs( add( delta( sub( sale, cogs ), 1 ), add( recch, invch ) ) ), lag( xrd, 1 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: R&D Cut with Slower Intangible Amortization
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms cutting R&D while reducing depreciation and amortization recognition relative to their identifiable intangible base subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Scaling depreciation and amortization by the combined expense and non-goodwill intangible base focuses on recognition intensity rather than the mechanical asset-mix behavior of dp divided by total assets. The interaction identifies simultaneous reductions in immediate R&D expense and subsequent amortization burden, a sharper dual expense-deferral mechanism than a simple trend substitution.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( winsor( delta( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ), rank( neg( winsor( delta( ratio( dp, add( dp, max( sub( intan, gdwl ), 0 ) ) ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capitalization Migration without Amortization
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1), 1))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MAX(DELTA(SUB(intan, gdwl), 1), 0), at), 1))), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(dp, ADD(dp, MAX(SUB(intan, gdwl), 0))), 1), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms shifting from expensed R&D toward identifiable-intangible capitalization while also reducing amortization recognition subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The migration gate requires both an R&D cut and positive non-goodwill intangible growth, while the final leg tests whether the newly capitalized base receives a correspondingly lower expense-recognition rate. This isolates delayed recognition within a changing accounting regime without relying on a generic total-accrual anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( rank( neg( winsor( delta( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( max( delta( sub( intan, gdwl ), 1 ), 0 ), at ), 1 ) ) ), rank( neg( winsor( delta( ratio( dp, add( dp, max( sub( intan, gdwl ), 0 ) ) ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital-Invariant Innovation Realization
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)), MIN(RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, recch), invch), at), 1), 3)), RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(recch, invch)), sale), 1), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms that exhibit both strong pre-working-capital cash generation and strong accrual-adjusted gross margins subsequently earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Receivables and inventory enter the two realization measures with opposite adjustments, so requiring both to be strong prevents a working-capital movement from mechanically creating a favorable score. The minimum operator implements a weakest-link test of whether innovation produces both economic margin and underlying cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ), min( rank( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, recch ), invch ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ), rank( ma( winsor( ratio( add( sub( sale, cogs ), add( recch, invch ) ), sale ), 1 ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Addback-Free Innovation Cash
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms with strong operating cash after removing the cash-flow-statement depreciation addback subsequently earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Subtracting dpc isolates cash support that does not depend on adding back a noncash depreciation and amortization charge. This tests whether innovation is supported by underlying cash earnings rather than applying another working-capital adjustment or downside operator to the archived cash-floor signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ), rank( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, dpc ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ) )
